def datetime_attribute_timeseries(
    time_index: pd.DatetimeIndex | TimeSeries,
    attribute: str,
    one_hot: bool = False,
    cyclic: bool = False,
    until: int | str | pd.Timestamp | None = None,
    add_length: int = 0,
    dtype=np.float64,
    with_columns: list[str] | str | None = None,
    tz: TimeZone = None,
) -> TimeSeries:
    """
    Returns a new TimeSeries with index `time_index` and one or more dimensions containing
    (optionally one-hot encoded or cyclic encoded) pd.DatatimeIndex attribute information derived from the index.

    1-indexed attributes are shifted to enforce 0-indexing across all the encodings.

    Parameters
    ----------
    time_index
        Either a `pd.DatetimeIndex` attribute which will serve as the basis of the new column(s), or
        a `TimeSeries` whose time axis will serve this purpose.
    attribute
        An attribute of `pd.DatetimeIndex`, or `week` / `weekofyear` / `week_of_year` - e.g. "month", "weekday", "day",
        "hour", "minute", "second". See all available attributes `here
        <https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/reference/api/pandas.DatetimeIndex.html#pandas.DatetimeIndex>`__.
    one_hot
        Boolean value indicating whether to add the specified attribute as a one hot encoding
        (results in more columns).
    cyclic
        Boolean value indicating whether to add the specified attribute as a cyclic encoding.
        Alternative to one_hot encoding, enable only one of the two.
        (adds 2 columns, corresponding to sin and cos transformation)
    until
        Extend the time_index up until timestamp for datetime indexed series
        and int for range indexed series, should match or exceed forecasting window.
    add_length
        Extend the time_index by add_length, should match or exceed forecasting window.
        Set only one of until and add_length.
    dtype
        The desired NumPy dtype (np.float32 or np.float64) for the resulting series
    with_columns
        Optionally, specify the output component names.

        - If `one_hot` and `cyclic` are ``False``, must be a string
        - If `cyclic` is ``True``, must be a list of two strings. The first string for the sine, the second for the
          cosine component name.
        - If `one_hot` is ``True``, must be a list of strings of the same length as the generated one hot encoded
          features.
    tz
        Optionally, a time zone to convert the time index before computing attributes.
        Supports any type handled by pandas
        `tz_convert <https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/reference/api/pandas.DatetimeIndex.tz_convert.html>`__.

    Returns
    -------
    TimeSeries
        New datetime attribute TimeSeries instance.
    """

    time_index_ts, time_index = _process_time_index(
        time_index=time_index,
        tz=tz,
        until=until,
        add_length=add_length,
    )

    if not (
        hasattr(pd.DatetimeIndex, attribute)
        or (attribute in ["week", "weekofyear", "week_of_year"])
    ):
        raise_log(
            ValueError(
                f"attribute `{attribute}` needs to be an attribute of pd.DatetimeIndex. "
                "See all available attributes in "
                "https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/reference/api/pandas.DatetimeIndex.html#pandas.DatetimeIndex"
            ),
        )

    if one_hot and cyclic:
        raise_log(ValueError("set only one of one_hot or cyclic to true"))

    num_values_dict = {
        "month": 12,
        "day": 31,
        "weekday": 7,
        "dayofweek": 7,
        "day_of_week": 7,
        "hour": 24,
        "minute": 60,
        "second": 60,
        "microsecond": 1000000,
        "nanosecond": 1000,
        "quarter": 4,
        "dayofyear": 365,
        "day_of_year": 365,
        "week": 52,
        "weekofyear": 52,
        "week_of_year": 52,
    }

    if attribute not in ["week", "weekofyear", "week_of_year"]:
        values = getattr(time_index, attribute)
    else:
        values = (
            time_index.isocalendar()
            .set_index("week")
            .index.astype("int64")
            .rename("time")
        )

    # shift 1-indexed datetime attributes
    if attribute in ONE_INDEXED_FREQS:
        values -= 1

    # leap years insert an additional day on the 29th of February
    if attribute in {"dayofyear", "day_of_year"} and any(time_index.is_leap_year):
        num_values_dict[attribute] += 1

    # years contain an additional week if they are :
    # - a regular year starting on a thursday
    # - a leap year starting on a wednesday
    if attribute in {"week", "weekofyear", "week_of_year"}:
        years = time_index.year.unique()
        # check if year respect properties
        additional_week_year = any(
            ((not first_day.is_leap_year) and first_day.day_name() == "Thursday")
            or (first_day.is_leap_year and first_day.day_name() == "Wednesday")
            for first_day in [pd.Timestamp(f"{year}-01-01") for year in years]
        )
        # check if time index actually include the additional week
        additional_week_in_index = time_index[-1] - time_index[0] + pd.Timedelta(
            days=1
        ) >= pd.Timedelta(days=365)

        if additional_week_year and additional_week_in_index:
            num_values_dict[attribute] += 1

    if one_hot or cyclic:
        if attribute not in num_values_dict:
            raise_log(
                ValueError(
                    f"Given datetime attribute `{attribute}` not supported with one-hot or cyclical encoding. "
                    f"Supported datetime attribute: {list(num_values_dict.keys())}."
                ),
            )

    if one_hot:
        values_df = pd.get_dummies(values)
        # fill missing columns (in case not all values appear in time_index)
        attribute_range = np.arange(num_values_dict[attribute])
        is_missing = np.isin(attribute_range, values_df.columns.values, invert=True)
        # if there are attribute_range columns that are
        # not in values_df.columns.values
        if is_missing.any():
            dict_0 = {i: False for i in attribute_range[is_missing]}
            # Make a dataframe from the dictionary and concatenate it
            # to the values values_df  in which the existing columns
            values_df = pd.concat(
                [values_df, pd.DataFrame(dict_0, index=values_df.index)], axis=1
            ).sort_index(axis=1)
        else:
            values_df = values_df[attribute_range]

        if with_columns is None:
            with_columns = [
                attribute + "_" + str(column_name) for column_name in values_df.columns
            ]

        if len(with_columns) != len(values_df.columns):
            raise_log(
                ValueError(
                    "For the given case with `one_hot=True`,`with_columns` must be a list of strings of length "
                    f"{values_df.columns}."
                ),
            )

        values_df.columns = with_columns
    else:
        if cyclic:
            if attribute == "day":
                periods = time_index.days_in_month.values
                freq = 2 * np.pi * np.reciprocal(periods.astype(dtype))
            else:
                period = num_values_dict[attribute]
                freq = 2 * np.pi / period

            if with_columns is None:
                with_columns = [attribute + "_sin", attribute + "_cos"]

            if len(with_columns) != 2:
                raise_log(
                    ValueError(
                        "`with_columns` must be a list of two strings when `cyclic=True`. "
                        "The first string for the sine component name, the second for the cosine component name."
                    ),
                )
            values_df = pd.DataFrame({
                with_columns[0]: np.sin(freq * values),
                with_columns[1]: np.cos(freq * values),
            })
        else:
            if with_columns is None:
                with_columns = attribute
            if not isinstance(with_columns, str):
                raise_log(
                    ValueError(
                        "`with_columns` must be a string specifying the output component name."
                    ),
                )
            values_df = pd.DataFrame({with_columns: values})
    return TimeSeries(
        times=time_index_ts,
        values=values_df.values.astype(dtype),
        components=values_df.columns,
        copy=False,
    )

 ('onehot wc', lambda: f(idx,'month',one_hot=True,with_columns=['a'])),

 ('list index', lambda: f(list(idx),'month')),
 ('range ts', lambda: f(TimeSeries.from_values(np.arange(3.)),'month')),

 ('until early', lambda: f(idx,'month',until='2019-12-30')),
 ('neg add_length', lambda: f(idx,'month',add_length=-2)),
]
for name, fn in cases:
    try:

        print(name, 'NO ERROR')

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pytest

from darts import TimeSeries
from darts.utils.timeseries_generation import datetime_attribute_timeseries

DAILY_START = "2020-01-01"
DAILY_LENGTH = 10


def daily_index(start=DAILY_START, periods=DAILY_LENGTH, freq="D", name=None):
    return pd.date_range(start, periods=periods, freq=freq, name=name)


def values_of(ts):
    """Return the (n_timesteps, n_components) float matrix of a `TimeSeries`."""
    return ts.all_values()[:, :, 0]


def hours_index(periods=6):
    return pd.date_range("2020-03-01 00:00", periods=periods, freq="h")


#############################
# plain (un-encoded) output #
#############################


def test_plain_returns_univariate_timeseries_with_expected_metadata():
    idx = daily_index()
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "month")

    assert isinstance(ts, TimeSeries)
    assert ts.n_components == 1
    assert list(ts.components) == ["month"]
    assert ts.dtype == np.float64
    assert ts.time_index.equals(idx)
    assert ts.freq == idx.freq
    assert values_of(ts).shape == (len(idx), 1)
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(
        values_of(ts).ravel(), (idx.month - 1).to_numpy().astype(float)
    )


def test_plain_values_track_time_index():
    idx = pd.date_range("2020-02-27", periods=4, freq="D")
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "month")

    # February is month 2 -> 0-indexed 1; then March starts -> 2
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values_of(ts).ravel(), [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0])


def test_accepts_timeseries_as_time_index():
    idx = daily_index()
    input_ts = TimeSeries.from_times_and_values(idx, np.arange(len(idx), dtype=float))
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(input_ts, "month")

    assert ts.time_index.equals(idx)
    assert list(ts.components) == ["month"]
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(
        values_of(ts).ravel(), (idx.month - 1).to_numpy().astype(float)
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "attribute",
    ["month", "day", "quarter", "dayofyear", "day_of_year"],
)
def test_one_indexed_attributes_are_shifted_to_zero_index(attribute):
    idx = daily_index(periods=70)
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, attribute)

    expected = np.asarray(getattr(idx, attribute)) - 1
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values_of(ts).ravel(), expected.astype(float))
    # 0-indexing: the minimum observed value must never be negative
    assert values_of(ts).min() >= 0


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "attribute",
    ["weekday", "dayofweek", "day_of_week", "hour", "minute", "second"],
)
def test_zero_indexed_attributes_are_not_shifted(attribute):
    idx = pd.date_range("2020-05-04 00:00", periods=8, freq="h")
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, attribute)

    expected = np.asarray(getattr(idx, attribute))
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values_of(ts).ravel(), expected.astype(float))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("attribute", ["week", "weekofyear", "week_of_year"])
def test_week_attributes_are_iso_weeks_shifted_by_one(attribute):
    idx = daily_index(periods=40)
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, attribute)

    assert list(ts.components) == [attribute]
    expected = idx.isocalendar().week.to_numpy().astype("int64") - 1
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values_of(ts).ravel(), expected.astype(float))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [np.float64, np.float32])
def test_dtype_is_respected(dtype):
    idx = daily_index()
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "day", dtype=dtype)
    assert ts.dtype == dtype

    ts_cyclic = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "month", cyclic=True, dtype=dtype)
    assert ts_cyclic.dtype == dtype

    ts_one_hot = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "month", one_hot=True, dtype=dtype)
    assert ts_one_hot.dtype == dtype


def test_custom_component_name_for_plain_output():
    idx = daily_index()
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "month", with_columns="my_month")

    assert list(ts.components) == ["my_month"]
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(
        values_of(ts).ravel(), (idx.month - 1).to_numpy().astype(float)
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad_columns", [["a"], ["a", "b"], 1])
def test_non_string_with_columns_without_encoding_raises(bad_columns):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as err:
        datetime_attribute_timeseries(daily_index(), "month", with_columns=bad_columns)
    assert "`with_columns` must be a string" in str(err.value)


def test_index_name_is_preserved():
    idx = daily_index(name="time")
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "month")
    assert ts.time_index.name == "time"


def test_repeated_calls_are_independent():
    idx = daily_index()
    first = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "day")
    second = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "day")

    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values_of(first), values_of(second))
    # the input index must not have been modified in place
    assert (idx.day == 1).all()


#############################
#        one hot encoding   #
#############################


def test_one_hot_month_layout():
    idx = daily_index()
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "month", one_hot=True)

    assert ts.n_components == 12
    assert list(ts.components) == [f"month_{i}" for i in range(12)]
    values = values_of(ts)
    assert values.shape == (len(idx), 12)
    # every timestep is encoded exactly once
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values.sum(axis=1), np.ones(len(idx)))
    # January is index 0
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values[:, 0], np.ones(len(idx)))
    # one-hot column for the month of each timestep is set
    for i, month in enumerate(idx.month - 1):
        assert values[i, month] == 1.0


def test_one_hot_fills_columns_absent_from_the_index():
    # February 2020 has 29 days -> day values 0..28, days 29 and 30 never appear
    idx = pd.date_range("2020-02-01", periods=5, freq="D")
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "day", one_hot=True)

    assert ts.n_components == 31
    assert list(ts.components) == [f"day_{i}" for i in range(31)]
    values = values_of(ts)
    # the two missing days are present as all-zero columns
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values[:, 29], np.zeros(len(idx)))
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values[:, 30], np.zeros(len(idx)))
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values.sum(axis=1), np.ones(len(idx)))


def test_one_hot_columns_are_sorted_numerically():
    idx = pd.date_range("2020-03-01", periods=3, freq="D")
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "month", one_hot=True)

    assert ts.n_components == 12
    assert list(ts.components) == [f"month_{i}" for i in range(12)]
    values = values_of(ts)
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values[:, 2], np.ones(3))
    assert values.sum() == 3.0


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "attribute,n_components",
    [
        ("month", 12),
        ("quarter", 4),
        ("day", 31),
        ("weekday", 7),
        ("dayofweek", 7),
        ("day_of_week", 7),
        ("hour", 24),
        ("minute", 60),
        ("second", 60),
        ("week", 52),
        ("weekofyear", 52),
        ("week_of_year", 52),
    ],
)
def test_one_hot_number_of_components(attribute, n_components):
    idx = daily_index(periods=2)
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, attribute, one_hot=True)

    assert ts.n_components == n_components
    assert list(ts.components) == [f"{attribute}_{i}" for i in range(n_components)]
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values_of(ts).sum(axis=1), np.ones(2))


def test_one_hot_dayofyear_has_366_columns_for_leap_year():
    leap = datetime_attribute_timeseries(
        pd.date_range("2020-01-01", periods=40, freq="D"), "dayofyear", one_hot=True
    )
    assert leap.n_components == 366

    # 2020-02-29 is the 60th day of the year -> 59 in 0-indexed form
    values = values_of(leap)
    row = list(leap.time_index).index(pd.Timestamp("2020-02-29"))
    assert values[row, 59] == 1.0
    assert values[row].sum() == 1.0


def test_one_hot_dayofyear_has_365_columns_for_non_leap_year():
    non_leap = datetime_attribute_timeseries(
        pd.date_range("2019-01-01", "2019-12-31", freq="D"),
        "dayofyear",
        one_hot=True,
    )
    assert non_leap.n_components == 365


def test_one_hot_week_handles_years_with_53_iso_weeks():
    idx = pd.date_range("2015-01-01", periods=365, freq="D")
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "week", one_hot=True)

    # 2015 starts on a Thursday -> 53 ISO weeks
    assert ts.n_components == 53
    assert list(ts.components) == [f"week_{i}" for i in range(53)]
    values = values_of(ts)
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values.sum(axis=1), np.ones(len(idx)))
    # 2015-12-28 belongs to ISO week 53 -> 0-indexed 52
    row = list(ts.time_index).index(pd.Timestamp("2015-12-28"))
    assert values[row, 52] == 1.0


def test_one_hot_week_stays_at_52_columns_for_short_index():
    # the index does not span a full year, so no extra week column is added
    idx = pd.date_range("2015-01-01", periods=3, freq="D")
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "week", one_hot=True)
    assert ts.n_components == 52


def test_one_hot_custom_column_names():
    idx = daily_index()
    names = [f"m{i}" for i in range(12)]
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "month", one_hot=True, with_columns=names)

    assert list(ts.components) == names
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values_of(ts)[:, 0], np.ones(len(idx)))


def test_one_hot_wrong_number_of_custom_columns_raises():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as err:
        datetime_attribute_timeseries(
            daily_index(), "month", one_hot=True, with_columns=["a", "b"]
        )
    assert "`with_columns` must be a list of strings of length" in str(err.value)


#############################
#       cyclic encoding     #
#############################


def test_cyclic_hour_has_sin_and_cos_components():
    idx = hours_index(periods=8)
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "hour", cyclic=True)

    assert list(ts.components) == ["hour_sin", "hour_cos"]
    assert ts.n_components == 2
    values = values_of(ts)
    expected_sin = np.sin(2 * np.pi * np.arange(8) / 24)
    expected_cos = np.cos(2 * np.pi * np.arange(8) / 24)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(values[:, 0], expected_sin)

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pytest

from darts import TimeSeries
from darts.utils.timeseries_generation import datetime_attribute_timeseries

DAILY_START = "2020-01-01"
DAILY_LENGTH = 10


def daily_index(start=DAILY_START, periods=DAILY_LENGTH, freq="D", name=None):
    return pd.date_range(start, periods=periods, freq=freq, name=name)


def values_of(ts):
    """Return the (n_timesteps, n_components) float matrix of a `TimeSeries`."""
    return ts.all_values()[:, :, 0]


def hours_index(periods=6):
    return pd.date_range("2020-03-01 00:00", periods=periods, freq="h")


#############################
# plain (un-encoded) output #
#############################


def test_plain_returns_univariate_timeseries_with_expected_metadata():
    idx = daily_index()
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "month")

    assert isinstance(ts, TimeSeries)
    assert ts.n_components == 1
    assert list(ts.components) == ["month"]
    assert ts.dtype == np.float64
    assert ts.time_index.equals(idx)
    assert ts.freq == idx.freq
    assert values_of(ts).shape == (len(idx), 1)
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(
        values_of(ts).ravel(), (idx.month - 1).to_numpy().astype(float)
    )


def test_plain_values_track_time_index():
    idx = pd.date_range("2020-02-27", periods=4, freq="D")
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, "month")

    # February is month 2 -> 0-indexed 1; then March starts -> 2
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values_of(ts).ravel(), [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0])


def test_accepts_timeseries_as_time_index():
    idx = daily_index()
    input_ts = TimeSeries.from_times_and_values(idx, np.arange(len(idx), dtype=float))
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(input_ts, "month")

    assert ts.time_index.equals(idx)
    assert list(ts.components) == ["month"]
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(
        values_of(ts).ravel(), (idx.month - 1).to_numpy().astype(float)
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "attribute",
    ["month", "day", "quarter", "dayofyear", "day_of_year"],
)
def test_one_indexed_attributes_are_shifted_to_zero_index(attribute):
    idx = daily_index(periods=70)
    ts = datetime_attribute_timeseries(idx, attribute)

    expected = np.asarray(getattr(idx, attribute)) - 1
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values_of(ts).ravel(), expected.astype(float))
    # 0-indexing: the minimum observed value must never be negative
    assert values_of(ts).min() >= 0


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "attribute",
    ["weekday", "dayofweek", "day_of_week", "hour", "minute", "second"],
)
def test_zero_indexed_attributes_are_not_shifted(attribute):

    expected = np.asarray(getattr(idx, attribute))
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values_of(ts).ravel(), expected.astype(float))

    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values_of(ts).ravel(), expected.astype(float))

    # January is index 0

    assert list(ts.components) == [f"day_{i}" for i in range(31)]

    # the two missing days are present as all-zero columns

    np.testing.assert_array_equal(values[:, 30], np.zeros(len(idx)))

def test_one_hot_number_of_components(attribute, n_components):

    )

    np.testing.assert_allclose(values_of(ts)[:, 0], np.sin(freq * days))
